controls.hint: Move your mouse to turn the gull
controls.stageLabel: Grassland flyover. Move the pointer or press the left and right arrow keys to turn the gull.
controls.unsupported: This scene needs WebGL, which your browser has turned off. Try another browser to see the flyover.

howToPlay.intro: Press Play sound, open the settings button to set the mix you like, then leave it running while you study or work.
howToPlay.steer: Move your mouse over the scene, or touch it, to point the gull in a new direction. It turns slowly and keeps its own pace, so you only nudge the flight.
howToPlay.keys: Click the scene and use the left and right arrow keys if you prefer the keyboard.
howToPlay.river: The brook gets louder and moves from ear to ear as you fly near the river; headphones make this easy to hear.
howToPlay.background: The sound keeps playing in a background tab, and the picture pauses to save battery.

about.title: About This White Noise Generator
about.description: Every sound here is generated live in your browser instead of looping a recording, so there is no audible seam however long you listen. Mix the three layers to taste, keep the tab open while you work, and the sound carries on in the background. The scenery is generated too: a winding river with the occasional fish, dirt roads and wooden bridges, grazing cattle and passing clouds, with the frame rate kept low to save battery.

sounds.title: Which Focus Sound Should You Use?

wind.name: Wind
wind.description: A soft, shifting hiss with slow gusts. It suits reading and writing when complete silence feels too quiet.

stream.name: Brook
stream.description: Running water with small bubbles. The gentle variation keeps it pleasant over long sessions, and it grows louder as you fly near the river.

deep.name: Brown noise
deep.description: A deep, steady rumble that covers voices, traffic and household noise better than brighter white noise. A common choice for long study sessions.
